reason: Sunlight can lift ocean water through evaporation, which seems a useful start to the water cycle.
expectation: I expect evaporation or water vapour, though the game may represent it differently.

alternatives.reason: Air might also help move water, but the Sun seems the clearer source of evaporation.

effect: Evaporation confirms the first step toward moving ocean water into the sky.
reaction: The result was expected, though it gave little detail.
reason: Air may carry or cool the evaporated water, advancing the water cycle.
expectation: I expect water vapour to gather into clouds, although the result may be an intermediate stage.

alternatives.reason: Ocean and air might also move water, but following evaporation seems more direct.

effect: Clouds confirms that cooling moist air condenses water into droplets or ice, suggesting rain is next.
reaction: The distinction between invisible vapour and visible cloud droplets is useful.
reason: Combining clouds with water seems the most direct route toward rainfall and rivers.
expectation: I expect rain or a rain-bearing cloud, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The Sun might drive another part of the cycle, but water seems more directly connected to rain.

effect: Rainfall brings water to land, suggesting it can now flow over the stone crust.
reaction: The progression from condensation to falling droplets is clear, though predictable.
reason: Rainfall on the crust seems the most direct way to start water flowing toward a river.
expectation: I expect runoff or an early stream, though it may first collect in hollows.

alternatives.reason: Sunlight and clouds might contribute to the cycle, but rainfall on land seems more relevant to the river goal.

effect: Rivers show how gravity moves water downhill and how erosion and deposition alter its route; the delta goal is now closer.
reaction: The connection between river flow and changing landscapes is useful.
reason: Combining rivers with earth may bring sediment into the process of building a delta.
expectation: I expect sediment transport or a delta-related intermediate, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Sunlight might help keep water cycling, but the delta goal seems more immediate.

effect: Sediment suggests the next step is depositing river-carried material where it meets the ocean.
reaction: The result was expected and gives a clear next step.
reason: Sediment entering the ocean could accumulate to build a delta.
expectation: I expect a delta or a related deposit, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Rivers and sunlight might address the continuing water cycle, but I want to pursue the delta first.

effect: The delta completes one goal; keeping water travelling remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see sediment become new land as the river slows.
reason: Sunlight can evaporate river water, potentially continuing the water cycle.
expectation: I expect evaporation from rivers or a representation of the continuing water cycle, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Clouds and sunlight might also represent part of the cycle, but evaporation from rivers seems more direct.

effect: The water cycle ties evaporation, condensation, precipitation and runoff together, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The roles of sunlight and gravity make the completed cycle satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the delta was most worthwhile: the result explains how sediment settles as a river slows and can form new land.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating evaporation was a predictable start and gave little detail on its own.

surprise.text: The distinction between invisible water vapour and the droplets or ice crystals in visible clouds sharpened my understanding.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the offered combinations had understandable purposes, though compatibility was provided by the menu rather than discovered.

continue.text: Yes. The concise explanations connecting combinations to real processes make another chapter appealing, even though some steps were predictable.
